query: In conventional alloys, loss of toughness has long been associated with grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation. By contrast, compositionally complex high-entropy alloys can suppress rapid grain coarsening and deleterious intermetallic formation and have shown favorable strength–ductility combinations and resistance to high-temperature softening and low-temperature embrittlement. These findings do not establish what governs possible toughness degradation in an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy. Under the constraint of retaining a compositionally complex alloy suitable for demanding engineering service, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains whether and why brittle behavior emerges? Specify a controlled comparison that would distinguish the hypothesis from conventional-alloy expectations, predicted observations relative to the initial baseline, its service and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification outcome.

generation.hypothesis: In compositionally complex high-entropy alloys (HEAs), brittle behavior under service conditions emerges not by the formation of coarse intermetallic precipitates, as in conventional alloys, but rather through subtle, nanoscale grain boundary segregation. Under prolonged exposure to service-relevant temperatures, specific alloying elements diffuse and minimally segregate at grain boundaries, leading to local chemical fluctuations and incipient short-range ordering that reduce interfacial cohesion, thereby promoting brittle fracture.
generation.material_initial_state: A single-phase high-entropy alloy produced by rapid solidification and homogenized through solution treatment; the as-cast microstructure exhibits a uniform dispersion of multiple principal elements with no detectable secondary phases or coarse precipitates.
generation.intervention: Subject the HEA to controlled thermal aging at temperatures representative of high-temperature service (e.g., 700–900°C) for times sufficient to promote elemental diffusion and grain boundary segregation. Simultaneously, a conventional alloy known to embrittle by forming coarse, brittle grain-boundary precipitates is treated under the identical conditions.
generation.conditions: Thermal aging performed in an inert (e.g., argon) atmosphere at 700–900°C for durations reflecting long-term exposure. Subsequent mechanical testing is carried out using impact (e.g., Charpy) and tensile tests at both ambient and low temperatures typical of service (to accentuate brittle behavior). Detailed microstructural characterization (using transmission electron microscopy and atom probe tomography) is conducted post-thermal treatment.
generation.structural_mediator: Nanoscale grain boundary segregation leading to localized compositional fluctuations and subtle short-range ordering at the grain boundaries.
generation.mechanism: High-temperature exposure drives differential diffusion of the multiple alloying species in the HEA; specific elements accumulate at the grain boundaries even without forming obvious precipitates. This minor segregation lowers the cohesive strength at the boundaries, resulting in brittle fracture under mechanical loading. This differs from conventional alloys where coarse, brittle intermetallic particles form and are readily detected.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the baseline as-cast HEA (which features a homogeneous, ductile microstructure), thermally aged HEA samples are predicted to exhibit lower toughness (as measured by decreased impact energy and a transition in fracture surfaces from ductile dimple patterns to brittle cleavage features). In contrast, the conventional alloy will show a distinctly different pattern with coarse intermetallic precipitates along grain boundaries. Nanoscale characterization should reveal clear, albeit subtle, segregation in the HEA that correlates with the observed decrease in toughness.
generation.baseline: The baseline is the as-cast or solution-treated single-phase HEA that displays a homogeneous microstructure and favorable strength–ductility performance with no signs of grain boundary embrittlement.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis is expected to hold under service-like conditions such as high-temperature aging (700–900°C) and mechanical loading regimes that promote brittle fracture (e.g., low-temperature impact tests). It may not apply if the alloy is operated outside of these thermal/or mechanical window boundaries or if service conditions limit the extent of grain boundary diffusion.
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty about which specific elemental species are most prone to segregation and the exact kinetics of this interfacial diffusion. Variations in composition and microstructural state may also influence the degree of segregation and the embrittlement threshold.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare matched samples of the HEA and a conventional alloy. Subject both to identical thermal aging conditions (700–900°C in an inert atmosphere over a specified duration). After treatment, perform microstructural analyses using high-resolution techniques (TEM, atom probe tomography) to detect grain boundary segregation and ordering in the HEA, and compare with the precipitation behavior in the conventional alloy. Execute mechanical tests (Charpy impact and tensile tests at ambient and subzero temperatures) to document differences in toughness and fracture modes.
measurements: Quantification of grain boundary element distribution (via atom probe tomography or EDS in TEM)
Fractography analysis (identification of brittle versus ductile fracture features)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis will be falsified if (a) the HEA does not exhibit any meaningful grain boundary segregation or incipient short-range ordering after thermal aging, or (b) its toughness and fracture behavior remain unchanged compared to the as-cast baseline, despite the applied thermal treatment. Likewise, if the conventional alloy and HEA show similar microstructural evolution (e.g., both forming coarse precipitates), that would also refute the proposed distinguishing mechanism.
